description: Found by the fz-go4.27 sweep, INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED by its correctness audit (at 2b431a3dd). Fixture map_pattern_binding_flows_into_selected_leaf (fixtures2, port_type_infer_test.rs): pick(%{id:x}) binds x; pick(:none) -> :none; pick(_) -> :unreachable is a DEAD catch-all (fixture comment: 'keeps the catch-all from contributing'). Expected main/0 return {int, :none}; ACTUAL {int | :unreachable, :none}. The dead catch-all leaks :unreachable into the FIRST tuple position but NOT the second (which correctly excludes it) — an ASYMMETRIC/positional leak, strengthening that this is a genuine defect in map-pattern proof narrowing (a clause proven dead should contribute nothing). The audit reproduced the exact {int|:unreachable, :none} by mutation. TASK: fix map-pattern narrowing so a provably-dead catch-all clause contributes to NO position (match the second-position behavior); then fill the port test TODO with {int, :none}. Likely related to how map-pattern reachability/deadness is proven vs how tuple-position return types are assembled.
title: Dead catch-all clause leaks :unreachable into first tuple position (map-pattern proof narrowing)
